title: Avocado Cannon vs Damaged Helmet
description: The player controls a cannon that launches avocados at a floating damaged helmet acting as a boss enemy. Each successful hit cracks the helmet further by changing its material properties, and the player must land 6 precise hits from different angles while the helmet orbits and dodges. A score panel and hit counter track progress toward destroying the helmet.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an avocado cannon game targeting a damaged helmet boss. Load Avocado.glb and DamagedHelmet.glb using GLTFLoader. Setup: Place a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 3, 12) looking at the origin. Add a directional light at (5, 10, 7) intensity 2, an ambient light intensity 0.5, and a dark starfield background using a large sphere with emissive point materials. The DamagedHelmet floats at the origin and continuously orbits in a figure-eight pattern using sine/cosine functions on x and y axes. Scale the Avocado to 15x its loaded size and the helmet to 3x. Interaction: The player clicks anywhere on the screen to fire an avocado projectile from the camera position toward the click point (use Raycaster to determine direction). The avocado travels as a physics projectile with slight gravity (y velocity decreasing over time). Implement collision detection using bounding spheres between each flying avocado and the helmet. On each hit: increment a hit counter (displayed as HTML overlay), flash the helmet red briefly using emissive material change, increase the helmet roughness by 0.12 and decrease metalness by 0.15 to simulate damage, and slightly increase the helmet orbit speed making it harder to hit. The player must also rotate the cannon angle using A/D keys which orbit the camera around the scene center on the xz plane. After 6 successful hits, display a victory screen overlay saying 'Helmet Destroyed!' with a restart button. Limit the player to 15 total avocado shots displayed as ammo count in the HUD. If ammo runs out before 6 hits, show a 'Game Over' screen with a retry button. Add an HTML overlay HUD showing: hits (0/6), ammo remaining, and a crosshair div centered on screen. Use OrbitControls only for initial scene preview, disable them once the game starts via a 'Start Game' button. Animate everything in a requestAnimationFrame loop. Ensure all avocado projectiles are removed from the scene after 4 seconds if no collision occurs.
